The text a referent copies into a new e-mail to the person, with the key

mail_credential_ready_text.Rd

Proposed by the coordinator of the referents on 2026-11-19 and decided the same day: with written steps for the first sign-in many people get in who would not with the welcome alone, so the message with the key brings them ready, one text per language, for the referent to copy. It carries the person's first name, the key, the date of the first sign-in and the steps, and nothing of the context: no instance address, no project, no user name. Those reach the person in the welcome and, for the project, in My Projects when the access e-mail arrives; the text says where to find them. Key and context do not travel together.

Usage

mail_credential_ready_text(first_name, credential, deadline)

Arguments

first_name

The person's first name, from the row; missing or empty leaves the greeting without it. The referent fills the field, so white space inside it, a line break included, becomes one space: the greeting stays one line.

credential

What the account was born with.

deadline

The date of the first sign-in, from mail_first_signin_deadline(); NULL, NA or empty leaves the sentence on the date out.

Value

A list with it and en, each a character vector of lines, the delimiters included.

Details

The steps are those of the work instruction on the first sign-in, cut to what a person needs on the day, with three choices made there: a private window always, the second factor only with Microsoft Authenticator, through Verified IDs and Scan QR code, and Yes to Stay signed in?. A step more, decided on 2026-11-24 with the configuration of Entra: the self-service reset asks for two methods, Authenticator and an e-mail address confirmed with a code, and no longer accepts a phone, so after Authenticator the person gives an address of their own.

The two methods close as Entra closes them, seen on a test account on 2026-11-24: Authenticator, method 1 of 2, with Done, then method 2 of 2, the recovery address, with Next. The Italian text gives the Italian label with the English one in brackets where that test or the work instruction 00.06 shows it (Avanti, Fine, Metodo 2 di 2), and the English label alone elsewhere.

The sentence that says where the welcome is also says what to do if it is not there, whether it was lost, went to the junk folder or never arrived: write to the referent (decided on 2026-11-25). It is said once, where the welcome is named in full.

The ban on Skip for now opens step 4, before the instructions of the step (decided on 2026-11-25): the first page of the step is the one that offers it, and the ban comes before the person reads on.

Each text sits between two delimiter lines, because the line with the user name stands above it in the same message, and a referent copying by hand should know where to stop. The delimiters are not a bare ---, the line that separates the two languages of every message.
